scope: Local public-projection corrections supported by the 2026-09-07 source audit. This registry contains no private intake material.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Fraser Health acknowledgement and commitment following In Plain Sight
source_normalizations.organization: Fraser Health and Fraser Salish Regional Caucus
source_normalizations.summary: In December 2020, Fraser Health and the Fraser Salish Regional Caucus jointly accepted the In Plain Sight review's findings and committed to work with Indigenous partners on eliminating racism. This is an institutional response and commitment; it does not itself demonstrate that the commitments were completed.
source_normalizations.caution: The source responds to a B.C.-wide review and is not evidence of a Saskatchewan event.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Commentary on the In Plain Sight review of B.C. health care
source_normalizations.summary: This commentary discusses the In Plain Sight review and its B.C.-wide findings and recommendations on Indigenous-specific racism in health care. It is commentary about a review, not an official investigation issued by this publisher.
source_normalizations.caution: The original In Plain Sight report is the source for the review's formal findings.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Professional-regulator reference to the In Plain Sight review
source_normalizations.organization: College of Pharmacists of British Columbia
source_normalizations.summary: The College of Pharmacists of British Columbia links readers to In Plain Sight, the B.C. review of Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination in health care. The page is a reference to that review, not a separate investigation or finding by the College.
source_normalizations.caution: The original review remains the authoritative source for its findings.

source_normalizations.organization: College of Pharmacists of British Columbia
source_normalizations.summary: The College of Pharmacists of British Columbia links readers to In Plain Sight, the B.C. review of Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination in health care. The page is a reference to that review, not a separate investigation or finding by the College.
source_normalizations.caution: The original review remains the authoritative source for its findings.

source_normalizations.summary: The Alberta Human Rights Commission's initiatives report describes a 2018 nursing cultural-competency project intended to address discrimination affecting Indigenous people in Alberta's health system. It documents a funded initiative, not a finding about an individual care experience or implementation outcome.
source_normalizations.caution: The report concerns Alberta initiatives and should not be presented as B.C. evidence.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Research on racism in Alberta emergency care
source_normalizations.summary: A 2022 qualitative study of 16 Alberta emergency-department providers reported accounts of racist stereotyping, disrespect and barriers affecting First Nations patients. It is research evidence about emergency care, not an official investigation.
source_normalizations.caution: The study reports provider perspectives and does not establish findings about any particular patient encounter.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Research report on emergency-department triage in Alberta
source_normalizations.summary: University of Alberta reporting describes research finding that First Nations patients in Alberta emergency departments were triaged as less urgent than other patients. It is research reporting about Alberta emergency care, not a recommendation or action.
source_normalizations.caution: The source does not support a Saskatchewan location.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Journalism reporting research on Alberta emergency care
source_normalizations.summary: CBC reported on research linking racism and discrimination to First Nations patients leaving Alberta emergency departments before being seen or against medical advice. The article reports research findings and related public context; it is not an official investigation.
source_normalizations.caution: The source concerns Alberta emergency care; any separately reported complaint in the article is not treated here as a formal finding.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Scoping review of anti-Indigenous racism in Canadian health care
source_normalizations.summary: This scoping review maps research on anti-Indigenous racism in Canadian health care, including settings, populations and regions represented in the literature. It is nationwide research synthesis, not an official investigation or a finding about a single province.
source_normalizations.caution: Canadian scope is retained because the review does not establish a single provincial jurisdiction for this record.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Qualitative systematic review of primary health-care experiences in Canada
source_normalizations.organization: Health Promotion and Chronic Disease Prevention in Canada
source_normalizations.summary: This qualitative systematic review synthesizes published evidence on Indigenous peoples' primary health-care experiences across Canada. It identifies supportive experiences as well as discriminatory attitudes and systemic barriers, without assigning a single provincial location.
source_normalizations.caution: Author affiliation or a discovery query does not make this Canada-wide review Saskatchewan or Alberta evidence.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Qualitative systematic review of primary health-care experiences in Canada
source_normalizations.summary: The Public Health Agency of Canada published a peer-reviewed qualitative systematic review of Indigenous peoples' primary health-care experiences across Canada. It synthesizes 22 articles and is research evidence, not an official investigation or a Saskatchewan-specific finding.
source_normalizations.caution: Publication by a federal body does not make a literature review a formal finding.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: National survey on Indigenous peoples' childbirth experiences
source_normalizations.summary: University of British Columbia reporting describes a national survey of Indigenous peoples' experiences during pregnancy and childbirth. The survey is nationwide research evidence and is not an official investigation or a Saskatchewan-specific event record.
source_normalizations.caution: The record retains national scope because the source does not establish a single provincial jurisdiction.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Qualitative research on anti-Indigenous racism in rural B.C. primary care
source_normalizations.organization: Canadian Family Physician / Rural Coordination Centre of British Columbia
source_normalizations.summary: This qualitative research article examines anti-Indigenous racism reported through the Rural Site Visits Project in rural British Columbia primary care. It is research evidence about a broader pattern, not an official investigation.
source_normalizations.caution: The study's conclusions are limited to its research design and do not establish individual findings.

source_normalizations.evidence_type: Research on structural racism in pregnancy and childbirth care in B.C.
source_normalizations.summary: This research article examines structural racism and Indigenous peoples' experiences of pregnancy and childbirth care in British Columbia. It is systemic research evidence, not an official investigation or a finding about an individual experience.
source_normalizations.caution: The source supports British Columbia context; it should not be copied into Alberta or Saskatchewan solely because those provinces were searched.
